commitments.quote: It applies to all agreements under which Business Associate creates, receives, maintains or transmits Protected Health Information for or on behalf of Covered Entity (the "Underlying Agreements").
commitments.summary: The BAA applies to every agreement under which ExampleCo creates, receives, maintains or transmits PHI for Amazing Health System and its affiliated hospitals and clinics.
commitments.scope: All Underlying Agreements involving PHI of Amazing Health System and its affiliated hospitals and clinics.
commitments.deviation: The DPA applies only to processing of Customer Personal Data under the Agreement and has an order-of-precedence clause (11.1) under which the DPA controls. The BAA covers PHI across all Underlying Agreements but has no order-of-precedence clause. Inference: the BAA text does not say how a conflict with the standard DPA would be resolved.

commitments.quote: Business Associate may use and disclose PHI only as necessary to perform the Underlying Agreements, as required by law, or as permitted by this BAA.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo may use and disclose PHI only to perform the Underlying Agreements, as required by law, or as the BAA permits.
commitments.scope: All PHI, including limited data sets (Section 2.4).
commitments.deviation: The DPA limits processing to Customer's documented instructions, which include Customer's configuration of the Services. The BAA instead uses a HIPAA permitted-use standard tied to performing the Underlying Agreements or legal requirement. Inference: this also restricts any AI or model-training use of PHI beyond service performance, although the BAA has no express AI clause equivalent to DPA 8.1 or 8.3.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall limit its uses and disclosures of PHI to the minimum necessary.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must limit its uses and disclosures of PHI to the minimum necessary.
commitments.scope: All PHI, including limited data sets.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Business Associate may de-identify PHI only in accordance with the safe harbor method at 45 C.F.R. § 164.514(b)(2), and may use the de-identified information only to provide and improve the services under the Underlying Agreements.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo may de-identify PHI only by the HIPAA safe harbor method and may use the resulting data only to provide and improve the services under the Underlying Agreements.
commitments.scope: De-identification of PHI and use of the resulting de-identified information.
commitments.deviation: The DPA lets ExampleCo use aggregated or de-identified Usage Data to operate, secure and improve the Services, with no prescribed de-identification method. The BAA requires the safe harbor method only (not expert determination) and limits use to providing and improving the services under the Underlying Agreements. Operating and securing are not separately listed.

commitments.quote: Information de-identified in accordance with this Section 2.3 is not PHI and is not subject to this BAA.
commitments.summary: Information de-identified under the safe harbor method is not PHI and falls outside the BAA.
commitments.scope: Only information de-identified by the safe harbor method in compliance with Section 2.3 is excluded. Information de-identified by other means remains PHI.
commitments.deviation: The DPA excludes Usage Data, meaning aggregated or de-identified data that does not identify Customer or any person, with no method requirement. The BAA excludes only data de-identified by HIPAA safe harbor. The BAA does not exclude merely aggregated data.

commitments.quote: A limited data set under 45 C.F.R. § 164.514(e) is PHI for all purposes of this BAA.
commitments.summary: Limited data sets are treated as PHI for every purpose of the BAA, including reporting, residency and return or destruction.
commitments.scope: Limited data sets under 45 C.F.R. § 164.514(e).
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall comply with Subpart C of 45 C.F.R. Part 164 with respect to ePHI.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must comply with the HIPAA Security Rule for ePHI.
commitments.scope: ePHI.
commitments.deviation: The DPA commits only to the vendor-described Annex 2 measures, which ExampleCo may update if overall security is not materially reduced. The BAA requires full HIPAA Security Rule compliance, a regulatory standard ExampleCo cannot change unilaterally.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall not store, process or access PHI outside the United States.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must not store or process PHI outside the United States.
commitments.scope: All PHI, including limited data sets. Under Section 5.1, this restriction flows down to Subcontractors.
commitments.deviation: The DPA stores data at rest in the hosting region Customer selects. The BAA imposes a fixed United States-only requirement covering processing as well as storage.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall not store, process or access PHI outside the United States.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must not access PHI from outside the United States.
commitments.scope: All PHI, and by Section 5.1 flow-down, Subcontractor access as well.
commitments.deviation: The DPA permits personnel and Subprocessors to access data from outside the hosting region, including the Manila, Philippines support center, under the Annex 3 transfer mechanism. The BAA prohibits any access to PHI from outside the United States. Inference: Manila-based support could not access PHI.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall maintain HITRUST r2 certification for the systems that store or process PHI.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must maintain HITRUST r2 certification for systems that store or process PHI.
commitments.scope: Systems that store or process PHI.
commitments.deviation: The DPA commits to SOC 2 Type II and ISO/IEC 27001, or substantially equivalent successor standards. The BAA requires HITRUST r2 specifically and has no successor-standard substitution.

commitments.quote: "Security Incident" has the meaning given in 45 C.F.R. § 164.304, limited to incidents involving ePHI that Business Associate or its Subcontractors create, receive, maintain or transmit for Covered Entity.
commitments.summary: Security Incidents that must be reported are those defined by HIPAA, limited to incidents involving ePHI that ExampleCo or its Subcontractors handle for Covered Entity.
commitments.scope: Incidents involving ePHI handled by ExampleCo or its Subcontractors for Covered Entity. Per 45 C.F.R. § 164.304 (drawn from the regulation, not restated in the contract), this includes attempted as well as successful unauthorized access, use, disclosure, modification or destruction, or interference with system operations.
commitments.deviation: The DPA covers only breaches ExampleCo has confirmed that compromised Customer Personal Data, and excludes unsuccessful attempts. The BAA's Security Incident needs no confirmation and, by regulatory definition, includes attempted incidents. Section 4.2 handles unsuccessful attempts through standing notice.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall report to Covered Entity any Breach of Unsecured PHI without unreasonable delay and in no event later than ten (10) calendar days after Discovery.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must report any Breach of Unsecured PHI without unreasonable delay and no later than 10 calendar days after Discovery.

deadline.anchor: Discovery of the Breach, as defined in the HIPAA Rules. Per 45 C.F.R. § 164.410(a)(2) (drawn from the regulation), this is the first day the Breach is known to ExampleCo, or by reasonable diligence would have been known, to any workforce member or agent other than the person committing it.

commitments.recipient: Covered Entity's Privacy Office at privacy-office@ahs.example, with a copy to its Information Security Office at iso@ahs.example (Section 4.4).
commitments.scope: Breaches of Unsecured PHI as defined in the HIPAA Rules, including limited data sets, in any form. Electronic Breaches may also trigger the earlier 5-business-day Security Incident report under Section 4.2.
commitments.deviation: The DPA allows 72 hours after ExampleCo confirms a breach. The BAA allows 10 calendar days, which is longer. However, the clock starts at HIPAA Discovery, including constructive knowledge through reasonable diligence, rather than confirmation, so it can start much earlier. The BAA also covers non-electronic PHI.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall report to Covered Entity any Security Incident within five (5) business days after Business Associate becomes aware of it.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must report any Security Incident within 5 business days after becoming aware of it.

deadline.anchor: ExampleCo becoming aware of the Security Incident (actual awareness by Business Associate).

commitments.recipient: Covered Entity's Privacy Office at privacy-office@ahs.example, with a copy to its Information Security Office at iso@ahs.example (Section 4.4).
commitments.scope: Security Incidents involving ePHI handled by ExampleCo or its Subcontractors for Covered Entity (Section 1.2). Unsuccessful attempts are covered by standing notice. Inference: for an electronic Breach that is also a Security Incident, this deadline may expire before the 10-day Breach deadline. No term says which period controls.
commitments.deviation: The DPA has a single 72-hour deadline after a breach is confirmed. The BAA adds a separate 5-business-day report for any Security Incident from awareness, with no confirmation or compromise threshold.

commitments.quote: This Section 4.2 serves as notice of, and no further report is required for, unsuccessful attempts such as pings, port scans and blocked log-in attempts that do not result in unauthorized access to ePHI.
commitments.summary: The BAA itself serves as notice of unsuccessful attempts that do not lead to unauthorized access to ePHI, so no separate report of them is required.
commitments.scope: Unsuccessful attempts such as pings, port scans and blocked log-in attempts that do not result in unauthorized access to ePHI.
commitments.deviation: The DPA excludes unsuccessful attempts, including denial-of-service attacks, from the breach definition entirely. The BAA keeps them within Security Incidents but treats Section 4.2 as standing notice. Denial-of-service is not listed. Inference: an attempt that interferes with system operations may still require a report.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall report to Covered Entity any use or disclosure of PHI not provided for by this BAA within ten (10) calendar days after becoming aware of it.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must report any use or disclosure of PHI not permitted by the BAA within 10 calendar days after becoming aware of it.

deadline.anchor: ExampleCo becoming aware of the use or disclosure not provided for by the BAA.

commitments.recipient: Covered Entity's Privacy Office at privacy-office@ahs.example, with a copy to its Information Security Office at iso@ahs.example (Section 4.4).
commitments.scope: Any use or disclosure of PHI, including limited data sets, not provided for by the BAA, whether or not it is a Breach or Security Incident.
commitments.deviation: The DPA requires notice only of confirmed Personal Data Breaches, within 72 hours. The BAA separately requires reporting of any impermissible use or disclosure within 10 calendar days of awareness, with no security-breach or confirmation threshold.

commitments.quote: Reports under this Section 4 shall be made in writing to Covered Entity's Privacy Office at privacy-office@ahs.example, with a copy to its Information Security Office at iso@ahs.example.
commitments.summary: All Section 4 reports must be in writing to the Privacy Office, with a copy to the Information Security Office.
commitments.recipient: Covered Entity's Privacy Office at privacy-office@ahs.example, with a copy to its Information Security Office at iso@ahs.example.
commitments.scope: All reports under Section 4: Breaches, Security Incidents and impermissible uses or disclosures.
commitments.deviation: The DPA sends notice to the security contact designated in the administration console, or else the account owner. The BAA fixes two contractual email addresses and requires written reports, so console contacts alone would not satisfy it.

commitments.quote: A report of a Breach shall include, to the extent known, the identity of each individual affected, the PHI involved, the date of the Breach and of its Discovery, and the steps taken to mitigate it.
commitments.summary: A Breach report must include, to the extent known, each affected individual's identity, the PHI involved, the Breach and Discovery dates, and mitigation steps.
commitments.recipient: Covered Entity's Privacy Office at privacy-office@ahs.example, with a copy to iso@ahs.example.
commitments.scope: Reports of Breaches of Unsecured PHI.
commitments.deviation: The DPA notice describes the nature of the breach, the categories of data and the measures taken, plus further information as it becomes available. The BAA requires individual-level identification of affected persons and the Breach and Discovery dates. It has no express obligation to supplement information later.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall reimburse Covered Entity's reasonable costs of notifying individuals, regulators and the media of a Breach caused by Business Associate or its Subcontractors.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must reimburse Covered Entity's reasonable costs of notifying individuals, regulators and the media of a Breach caused by ExampleCo or its Subcontractors.
commitments.scope: Breaches caused by ExampleCo or its Subcontractors. Costs are limited to notification of individuals, regulators and the media.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall ensure that each Subcontractor that creates, receives, maintains or transmits PHI on its behalf agrees in writing to the same restrictions and conditions that apply to Business Associate under this BAA.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must ensure every Subcontractor handling PHI agrees in writing to the same restrictions and conditions as ExampleCo under the BAA.
commitments.scope: Each Subcontractor (45 C.F.R. § 160.103) that creates, receives, maintains or transmits PHI on ExampleCo's behalf. This includes the US-only, HITRUST and reporting terms, and would include AI model providers handling PHI (inference).
commitments.deviation: The DPA makes ExampleCo responsible for Subprocessors' performance, gives general authorization, and requires 30 days' notice with an objection right. The BAA requires written flow-down of identical restrictions but contains no subcontractor notice, list or objection mechanism.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall make PHI in a Designated Record Set available to Covered Entity within ten (10) business days after Covered Entity's request, so Covered Entity can meet 45 C.F.R. § 164.524.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must make PHI in a Designated Record Set available to Covered Entity within 10 business days of request so it can meet individual access obligations.

deadline.anchor: Covered Entity's request

commitments.scope: PHI in a Designated Record Set.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall make its internal practices, books and records relating to PHI available to the Secretary of Health and Human Services for purposes of determining compliance with the HIPAA Rules.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must make its internal practices, books and records relating to PHI available to the HHS Secretary for HIPAA compliance review.
commitments.recipient: Secretary of Health and Human Services
commitments.scope: Internal practices, books and records relating to PHI.
commitments.deviation: The DPA treats SOC 2 and penetration test reports as satisfying audit rights. Any further audit must be required by a supervisory authority and is limited to once per 12 months, on 60 days' notice, at Customer's expense. The BAA grants HHS access with no frequency, notice, expense or report-substitution limits.

commitments.quote: On termination of the Underlying Agreements, Business Associate shall return or destroy all PHI within thirty (30) days.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must return or destroy all PHI within 30 days after termination of the Underlying Agreements.

deadline.anchor: Termination of the Underlying Agreements

commitments.scope: All PHI, including limited data sets. The clause has no express backup carve-out.
commitments.deviation: The DPA deletes within 90 days after termination, with backups overwritten within a further 35 days, and offers no return option. The BAA requires return or destruction of all PHI within 30 days, with no separate backup period. The BAA has no counterpart to the DPA 10.2 deletion certification.

commitments.quote: If return or destruction is not feasible, Business Associate shall extend the protections of this BAA to that PHI for as long as it retains it.
commitments.summary: If PHI cannot feasibly be returned or destroyed, ExampleCo must keep applying the BAA's protections to it for as long as ExampleCo retains it.
commitments.scope: PHI whose return or destruction is not feasible. Inference: this may include backups not purged within 30 days.
commitments.deviation: The DPA has no infeasibility exception and no survival of protections for retained data. It relies on scheduled deletion and backup overwrite. The BAA extends all BAA protections indefinitely to any retained PHI.

commitments.quote: This Addendum controls over any conflicting term of the Agreement, any order form, and any data processing addendum, privacy policy, or other document published or provided by Supplier.
commitments.summary: The Addendum overrides any conflicting term in the Agreement, order forms, and any Supplier DPA, privacy policy or other Supplier document.
commitments.scope: All Supplier performance under the Agreement. This includes the ExampleCo standard DPA's breach, subprocessor, location, AI, audit and deletion terms wherever they conflict.
commitments.deviation: The DPA states that the DPA controls over the Agreement. Here the Bank Addendum controls over the Agreement and over any Supplier DPA, so the DPA's weaker terms (72-hour breach notice, 30-day subprocessor notice, offshore access, 90-day deletion) give way where they conflict.

commitments.quote: Terms incorporated by reference to a Supplier website, including any Supplier trust or security site, do not bind Bank and do not modify this Addendum.
commitments.summary: Terms incorporated by reference to a Supplier website or trust site do not bind Bank and cannot modify the Addendum.
commitments.scope: Any Supplier website terms, including the Trust Center (trust.exampleco.example).
commitments.deviation: The DPA relies on the Trust Center for the subprocessor list, subprocessor notices, SOC 2 access under NDA terms and pen test summaries. Under the Addendum, Trust Center terms do not bind Bank, and Trust Center postings do not replace the direct notices and deliveries the Addendum requires.

commitments.quote: "Bank Data" means all data and information, in any form, that Supplier or any Subcontractor receives, accesses, creates or processes in connection with the Agreement, including (a) data provided by or on behalf of Bank or its customers; (b) metadata, logs and configuration data relating to Bank's use of the Services; and (c) any data derived from any of the foregoing, including model outputs, embeddings, annotations, and data that has been aggregated, de-identified, pseudonymized or tokenized.
commitments.summary: Bank Data covers all data handled in connection with the Agreement, not only personal data, and includes metadata, logs, model outputs, embeddings and aggregated or de-identified derivatives.
commitments.scope: All data in any form, including metadata, logs, configuration data, model outputs, embeddings, annotations, and aggregated, de-identified, pseudonymized or tokenized derived data. It covers data of Bank and its Affiliates, including ANB Securities LLC.
commitments.deviation: The DPA covers only Customer Personal Data (DPA 2.1). It also excludes aggregated or de-identified Usage Data, which ExampleCo may use to improve the Services (DPA 8.2). Here that data is Bank Data, so every Addendum duty, including the AI restrictions, applies to it.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall maintain a written information security program that is consistent with the NIST Cybersecurity Framework and the FFIEC Information Technology Examination Handbook.
commitments.summary: Supplier must maintain a written information security program consistent with the NIST CSF and the FFIEC IT Examination Handbook.
commitments.deviation: The DPA commits only to the Annex 2 measures, which ExampleCo may update unilaterally. The Addendum requires a written program aligned to NIST CSF and FFIEC and has no unilateral update right.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall encrypt Bank Data at rest using AES-256 or stronger and in transit using TLS 1.2 or higher.
commitments.summary: Supplier must encrypt Bank Data at rest with AES-256 or stronger and in transit with TLS 1.2 or higher.
commitments.scope: All Bank Data, including derived and de-identified data.
commitments.deviation: The encryption standard is substantively the same as the DPA, but it applies to all Bank Data rather than Customer Data.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall require multi-factor authentication for all remote access to systems that store, process or transmit Bank Data.
commitments.summary: Supplier must require MFA for all remote access to systems that store, process or transmit Bank Data.
commitments.scope: All remote access to any system handling Bank Data.
commitments.deviation: The DPA requires MFA for access to production systems. The Addendum requires it for all remote access to any system that stores, processes or transmits Bank Data.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall complete a criminal background check on all Supplier Personnel before granting them access to Bank Data, to the extent permitted by law.
commitments.summary: Supplier must complete criminal background checks on all Supplier and Subcontractor personnel before they access Bank Data, where the law permits.
commitments.scope: Employees, contractors and agents of Supplier and of any Subcontractor.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall maintain throughout the term of the Agreement a current SOC 2 Type II report covering the Services.
commitments.summary: Supplier must keep a current SOC 2 Type II report covering the Services for the whole term.
commitments.deviation: The Addendum requires a current SOC 2 Type II report throughout the term. It does not require ISO/IEC 27001, and it does not allow substitution of successor standards.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall store and process Bank Data only within the United States.
commitments.summary: Supplier must store and process Bank Data only in the United States.
commitments.scope: All Bank Data, including derived data, logs and metadata.
commitments.deviation: The DPA limits only storage at rest, to a customer-selected region. The Addendum confines both storage and processing to the US.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall not permit any Supplier Personnel located outside the United States to access Bank Data, including for support or maintenance, without Bank's prior written approval.
commitments.summary: No Supplier or Subcontractor personnel outside the US may access Bank Data, including for support, without Bank's prior written approval.
commitments.scope: Personnel of Supplier and of any Subcontractor located outside the US.
commitments.deviation: The DPA permits access from outside the hosting region, including from the Manila support center. The Addendum prohibits offshore access without Bank's prior written approval.

commitments.quote: Supplier may permit only the Subcontractors listed in Schedule 2 ("Approved Subcontractors") to access Bank Data, and each only within the scope stated for it in Schedule 2.
commitments.summary: Only Schedule 2 Approved Subcontractors may access Bank Data, and each only within its listed scope.
commitments.scope: Subcontractor means any third party, including any Supplier Affiliate, that performs Services or has access to Bank Data.
commitments.deviation: The DPA gives general authorization based on the Trust Center list. The Addendum uses a closed list with per-subcontractor scope limits, and Supplier Affiliates are also covered.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall give Bank's Third-Party Risk Management office at least ninety (90) days' prior written notice, delivered as provided in Exhibit C, before adding or replacing any Subcontractor or expanding an Approved Subcontractor's scope.
commitments.summary: Supplier must give Bank's TPRM office at least 90 days' written notice before adding or replacing a Subcontractor or expanding an Approved Subcontractor's scope.

deadline.anchor: adding or replacing any Subcontractor or expanding an Approved Subcontractor's scope

commitments.recipient: Bank Third-Party Risk Management office, tprm-notices@anb.example, with a copy to Awesome National Bank, N.A., Legal Department, 100 Example Plaza, New York, NY 10001
commitments.scope: New or replacement Subcontractors and any expansion of an Approved Subcontractor's scope.
commitments.deviation: The DPA requires 30 days' notice via a Trust Center update and email to subscribers. The Addendum requires 90 days' direct written notice to TPRM with a copy to Legal, and it also covers scope expansions. It contains no counterpart to the DPA 5.4 urgent-replacement exception.

commitments.quote: Bank may object within thirty (30) days after receiving the notice. If Bank objects, Supplier shall not engage the Subcontractor for the Services provided to Bank, or Bank may terminate the affected Services without penalty and receive a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees.
commitments.summary: Bank may object within 30 days of receiving notice. If it does, Supplier must not use the Subcontractor for Bank, or Bank may terminate the affected Services without penalty and with a pro-rata refund.

deadline.anchor: Bank's receipt of the Subcontractor notice

commitments.deviation: The DPA gives 15 days, requires reasonable data protection grounds and makes termination the sole remedy. The Addendum gives 30 days with no grounds required. Supplier must not engage the objected Subcontractor for Bank, or Bank may terminate without penalty and receive a pro-rata refund.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall impose on each Subcontractor written obligations at least as protective of Bank Data as this Addendum.
commitments.summary: Supplier must flow down written obligations at least as protective as the Addendum to every Subcontractor.
commitments.scope: All Subcontractors, including Supplier Affiliates.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall require each Subcontractor to notify Supplier of any Security Incident within six (6) hours after the Subcontractor's Discovery.
commitments.summary: Supplier must contractually require each Subcontractor to notify Supplier of any Security Incident within 6 hours of the Subcontractor's Discovery.

deadline.anchor: the Subcontractor's Discovery: when the Subcontractor knew, or with reasonable diligence would have known, of the Security Incident

commitments.scope: Any actual or reasonably suspected Security Incident.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Supplier remains fully liable to Bank for the acts and omissions of its Subcontractors.
commitments.summary: Supplier is fully liable to Bank for its Subcontractors' acts and omissions.
commitments.deviation: The DPA makes ExampleCo responsible only for Subprocessors' performance of DPA obligations. The Addendum imposes full liability for all of their acts and omissions.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall notify Bank of any Security Incident as soon as possible and in no event later than twelve (12) hours after Discovery.
commitments.summary: Supplier must notify Bank of any Security Incident as soon as possible and no later than 12 hours after Discovery.

deadline.anchor: Discovery: the earliest time Supplier or any Subcontractor knew, or by exercising reasonable diligence would have known, of the Security Incident

commitments.recipient: Bank Cyber Fusion Center, telephone (24x7) +1 (212) 555-0147 and email cfc-thirdparty@anb.example
commitments.scope: Any actual or reasonably suspected unauthorized access to, use, disclosure, alteration or destruction of Bank Data. It also covers unauthorized access to any Supplier or Subcontractor system handling Bank Data, even if access to Bank Data is not confirmed.
commitments.deviation: The DPA allows 72 hours, counted from ExampleCo's confirmation of a breach of Customer Personal Data, and excludes unsuccessful attempts. The Addendum allows 12 hours, counted from the earliest actual or constructive knowledge of Supplier or any Subcontractor. It covers suspected incidents and system intrusions involving any Bank Data.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall give notice under Section 6.1 by telephone and by email to Bank's Cyber Fusion Center as provided in Exhibit C. Notice provided only to Bank's relationship manager, or through a Supplier status page or trust site, does not satisfy Section 6.1.
commitments.summary: Incident notice must go by both telephone and email to the Cyber Fusion Center. Notice only to the relationship manager or on a status page or trust site does not count.
commitments.recipient: Bank Cyber Fusion Center, telephone (24x7) +1 (212) 555-0147 and email cfc-thirdparty@anb.example (not the relationship manager Dana Okafor, dana.okafor@anb.example, who handles routine matters only)
commitments.deviation: The DPA sends notice to the security contact designated in the console, or else the account owner. The Addendum requires both telephone and email to the Cyber Fusion Center and excludes relationship-manager-only notice and status page or trust site notice.

commitments.quote: Supplier's initial notice shall include all information then known about the Security Incident, including the date and time of Discovery, the systems and Subcontractors involved, and the categories of Bank Data affected or potentially affected.
commitments.summary: The initial notice must include all information then known, including the Discovery time, the systems and Subcontractors involved, and the Bank Data categories affected or potentially affected.
commitments.deviation: The DPA requires the nature of the breach, the data categories and the measures taken. The Addendum requires all known information, including the Discovery date and time, the systems and Subcontractors involved, and potentially affected categories.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall provide written status updates at least once every twenty-four (24) hours until the Security Incident is contained
commitments.summary: Supplier must give written status updates at least every 24 hours until the incident is contained.

deadline.anchor: initial Security Incident notice, until containment

commitments.recipient: Bank Cyber Fusion Center (inference: Exhibit C lists the CFC for Section 6.1 notices; it names no separate contact for updates)
commitments.deviation: The DPA requires further information only as it becomes available. The Addendum requires fixed written updates every 24 hours until containment.

commitments.quote: and shall deliver a written root-cause report within thirty (30) days after containment.
commitments.summary: Supplier must deliver a written root-cause report within 30 days after containment.

deadline.anchor: containment of the Security Incident

commitments.recipient: Bank (inference: the Cyber Fusion Center, as the Section 6 incident contact)
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall not notify any Bank customer, regulator, law enforcement agency or the media of a Security Incident involving Bank Data without Bank's prior written consent, unless required by law.
commitments.summary: Supplier may not notify Bank customers, regulators, law enforcement or the media about a Security Incident without Bank's prior written consent unless the law requires it.
commitments.scope: Security Incidents involving Bank Data.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Where law requires such notice, Supplier shall inform Bank before giving it, to the extent legally permitted.
commitments.summary: Where the law requires third-party notice, Supplier must inform Bank before giving it, where legally permitted.

deadline.anchor: Supplier giving a legally required notice to a customer, regulator, law enforcement or the media (the contract sets no minimum period, only 'before')

commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall preserve all logs, images and other forensic evidence relating to a Security Incident for at least one (1) year after containment
commitments.summary: Supplier must preserve all logs, images and forensic evidence of a Security Incident for at least one year after containment.

deadline.anchor: containment of the Security Incident

commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: and shall give Bank and its designated forensic investigator access to that evidence on request.
commitments.summary: On request, Supplier must give Bank and its forensic investigator access to the preserved evidence.
commitments.recipient: Bank and its designated forensic investigator
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall reimburse Bank's reasonable costs of investigating and responding to a Security Incident caused by Supplier or any Subcontractor, including costs of notifying affected individuals and providing them with twenty-four (24) months of credit monitoring.
commitments.summary: Supplier must reimburse Bank's reasonable investigation and response costs for Security Incidents caused by Supplier or a Subcontractor, including individual notification and 24 months of credit monitoring.
commitments.scope: Security Incidents caused by Supplier or any Subcontractor.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Supplier's obligations to ANB Securities LLC are supplemented by Exhibit D.
commitments.summary: Exhibit D adds obligations toward ANB Securities LLC on top of the Addendum.
commitments.scope: ANB Securities LLC, a Bank Affiliate.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Where this Addendum, the Agreement, any exhibit or schedule, or applicable law specifies more than one period for the same notice, the shortest period applies.
commitments.summary: Where more than one period applies to the same notice, the shortest one governs.
commitments.scope: All notice periods in the Addendum, Agreement, exhibits, schedules and applicable law. As a result, the 12-hour period in 6.1 displaces the 72-hour period in Exhibit D.2 and the DPA's 72-hour period.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.summary: ExampleCo must maintain the Annex 2 Security Measures and may update them, provided updates do not materially reduce overall security.

commitments.quote: ExampleCo will maintain a SOC 2 Type II report and ISO/IEC 27001 certification for the Services, or successor standards that are substantially equivalent.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must maintain a SOC 2 Type II report and ISO/IEC 27001 certification for the Services, or substantially equivalent successor standards.

commitments.quote: Customer grants ExampleCo general authorization to engage Subprocessors. The current list of Subprocessors is published on the Trust Center.
commitments.summary: Customer gives ExampleCo general authorization to engage Subprocessors, and ExampleCo publishes the current list on the Trust Center.
commitments.scope: Subprocessors, meaning any third party engaged by ExampleCo that processes Customer Personal Data.

commitments.quote: ExampleCo will give notice of any new Subprocessor at least thirty (30) days before the new Subprocessor begins processing Customer Personal Data, by updating the Trust Center list and emailing Customers who have subscribed to Subprocessor updates on the Trust Center.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must give at least 30 days' notice of a new Subprocessor by updating the Trust Center list and emailing subscribed customers.

deadline.anchor: the new Subprocessor begins processing Customer Personal Data

commitments.recipient: Customers who have subscribed to Subprocessor updates on the Trust Center (trust.exampleco.example), by email, plus the published Trust Center list
commitments.scope: Inference: Customer receives an email only if it has subscribed on the Trust Center. Otherwise notice is only the Trust Center list update.

commitments.quote: Customer may object to a new Subprocessor on reasonable data protection grounds by written notice within fifteen (15) days after ExampleCo's notice. If the parties cannot resolve the objection within thirty (30) days, Customer may terminate the affected Services as its sole and exclusive remedy.
commitments.summary: Customer may object to a new Subprocessor in writing within 15 days of notice on reasonable data protection grounds, and if the objection is unresolved within 30 days, Customer's sole remedy is to terminate the affected Services.

deadline.anchor: ExampleCo's notice of the new Subprocessor

secondary_deadline.anchor: Customer's objection (inference: the contract does not state when the 30-day period starts)

commitments.quote: Where ExampleCo must replace a Subprocessor urgently to protect the security or continuity of the Services, ExampleCo may do so without prior notice and will notify Customer promptly afterward.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo may replace a Subprocessor urgently without prior notice to protect security or continuity, but must notify Customer promptly afterward.
commitments.scope: Urgent replacements needed to protect the security or continuity of the Services.

commitments.quote: ExampleCo remains responsible for its Subprocessors' performance of the obligations in this DPA.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo stays responsible for its Subprocessors' performance of the DPA obligations.

commitments.quote: Customer Personal Data will be stored at rest in the hosting region Customer selects for its Services.
commitments.summary: Customer Personal Data is stored at rest in the hosting region Customer selects.
commitments.scope: Covers storage at rest only. Access from other locations is permitted under Section 6.2.

commitments.quote: ExampleCo personnel and Subprocessors may access Customer Personal Data from locations outside the selected hosting region to provide support, maintenance and security operations, including from ExampleCo's support center in Manila, Philippines.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo personnel and Subprocessors may access Customer Personal Data from outside the selected hosting region, including from Manila, Philippines, for support, maintenance and security operations.
commitments.scope: Access for support, maintenance and security operations.

commitments.quote: Any transfer is made under the transfer mechanism in Annex 3.
commitments.summary: Any transfer of Customer Personal Data is made under the Annex 3 transfer mechanism.

commitments.quote: ExampleCo will notify Customer without undue delay, and in any event within seventy-two (72) hours, after ExampleCo confirms a Personal Data Breach.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must notify Customer of a Personal Data Breach without undue delay and within 72 hours after ExampleCo confirms it.

deadline.anchor: ExampleCo's confirmation of a Personal Data Breach (the clock starts on ExampleCo's own confirmation, not on discovery or suspicion)

commitments.recipient: Security contact designated by Customer in the Services administration console, or, if none is designated, Customer's account owner
commitments.scope: Confirmed Personal Data Breaches affecting Customer Personal Data. Unsuccessful attempts are excluded.

commitments.quote: ExampleCo will send notice to the security contact Customer designates in the Services administration console. If no security contact is designated, ExampleCo will send notice to Customer's account owner.
commitments.summary: Breach notices go to Customer's designated security contact in the admin console, or to the account owner if no contact is designated.
commitments.recipient: Security contact designated in the Services administration console. Fallback: Customer's account owner.

commitments.quote: ExampleCo's notice will describe, to the extent then known, the nature of the Personal Data Breach, the categories of data affected, and the measures taken or proposed to address it.
commitments.summary: The breach notice must describe, to the extent known, the nature of the breach, the categories of data affected and the measures taken or proposed.
commitments.recipient: Security contact designated in the Services administration console, or Customer's account owner

commitments.quote: ExampleCo will provide further information as it becomes available.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must provide further breach information as it becomes available.
commitments.recipient: Security contact designated in the Services administration console, or Customer's account owner (inference: the contract does not specify a recipient for updates)

commitments.quote: ExampleCo's notification of or response to a Personal Data Breach is not an acknowledgment of fault or liability.
commitments.summary: Notifying of or responding to a breach does not amount to ExampleCo admitting fault or liability.

commitments.quote: ExampleCo will not use Customer Data to train or fine-tune any foundation model that is made available to other customers.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo will not use Customer Data to train or fine-tune foundation models made available to other customers.
commitments.scope: Customer Data, not only personal data. Inference: the restriction does not cover models used only for Customer, non-foundation models, or Usage Data.

commitments.quote: ExampleCo may use Usage Data to operate, secure and improve the Services.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo may use Usage Data to operate, secure and improve the Services.
commitments.scope: Usage Data, meaning aggregated or de-identified data that does not identify Customer or any natural person.

commitments.quote: ExampleCo lists the third-party model providers used by AI features as Subprocessors on the Trust Center.
commitments.summary: Third-party AI model providers are listed as Subprocessors on the Trust Center.
commitments.scope: Inference: model providers are therefore covered by the Section 5 notice and objection process.

commitments.quote: ExampleCo requires its model providers not to retain prompts or outputs beyond the time needed to return a response, except as required for abuse monitoring.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo requires model providers not to retain prompts or outputs beyond the time needed to respond, except for abuse monitoring.
commitments.scope: Prompts and outputs of AI features. The abuse-monitoring exception has no stated time limit.

commitments.quote: ExampleCo will make its most recent SOC 2 Type II report available to Customer through the Trust Center, subject to Customer's acceptance of the Trust Center non-disclosure terms.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo will provide its latest SOC 2 Type II report through the Trust Center, once Customer accepts the Trust Center non-disclosure terms.

commitments.quote: ExampleCo will engage an independent third party to perform a penetration test of the Services at least annually and will make an executive summary of the results available through the Trust Center.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must have an independent third party penetration test the Services at least annually and publish an executive summary on the Trust Center.

deadline.anchor: penetration test of the Services

commitments.scope: Only an executive summary of the results is provided.

commitments.quote: Customer agrees that the reports in Sections 9.1 and 9.2 satisfy any audit right under Data Protection Laws. Where a supervisory authority requires a further audit, Customer may conduct one on-site audit per twelve (12) month period, with at least sixty (60) days' written notice, during business hours, and at Customer's expense.
commitments.summary: The SOC 2 report and pen test summary satisfy Customer's audit rights, and Customer may conduct one on-site audit per 12 months only when a supervisory authority requires it, with 60 days' written notice, during business hours, at Customer's expense.

deadline.anchor: the on-site audit

secondary_deadline.anchor: limit of one on-site audit per 12-month period

commitments.scope: On-site audits only where a supervisory authority requires a further audit.

commitments.quote: Within ninety (90) days after termination or expiry of the Agreement, ExampleCo will delete Customer Personal Data from the Services. Backups are overwritten in the ordinary course within a further thirty-five (35) days.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must delete Customer Personal Data from the Services within 90 days after the Agreement ends, and backups are overwritten within a further 35 days.

deadline.anchor: termination or expiry of the Agreement

commitments.scope: Customer Personal Data in the Services and in backups.

commitments.quote: ExampleCo will provide written certification of deletion upon Customer's written request.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must provide written certification of deletion when Customer requests it in writing.

commitments.quote: If this DPA conflicts with the Agreement, this DPA controls as to the processing of Customer Personal Data.
commitments.summary: Where the DPA conflicts with the Agreement, the DPA controls for the processing of Customer Personal Data.
commitments.scope: Limited to the processing of Customer Personal Data.

commitments.quote: Customer Data is encrypted at rest using AES-256 and in transit using TLS 1.2 or higher.
commitments.summary: Customer Data is encrypted at rest with AES-256 and in transit with TLS 1.2 or higher.
commitments.scope: Customer Data.

commitments.quote: Access to production systems requires multi-factor authentication.
commitments.summary: Access to production systems requires multi-factor authentication.

commitments.quote: ExampleCo maintains a business continuity and disaster recovery plan and tests it at least annually.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo maintains a business continuity and disaster recovery plan and tests it at least annually.

deadline.anchor: testing of the business continuity and disaster recovery plan

commitments.quote: Transfers of Customer Personal Data subject to EU or UK Data Protection Laws are made under the Standard Contractual Clauses, Module 2 or Module 3 as applicable.
commitments.summary: Transfers of Customer Personal Data subject to EU or UK law are made under the Standard Contractual Clauses, Module 2 or 3.
commitments.scope: Transfers subject to EU or UK Data Protection Laws. Inference: no mechanism is stated for other transfers.
